title: Release lore-cli 0.15.0 paired with quest-cli 0.15.0, carrying LCLI-771/751/774 (ODOC-556)
description: Release-cut task for the paired 0.15.0 release (Article 3: lore and quest are one unit), leader decision 2026-10-31; amended 2026-11-01 from the 0.14.2 patch originally filed, see the dec-0kfl7kc note (ODOC-556 semver ruling: the Codex skill path move is breaking). Scope is ODOC-556 only: LCLI-771 (Codex skill under .agents/skills, bare-init notice), LCLI-751 (release gate probe re-based onto it) and LCLI-774 (notice wording). Follows the release-publishing runbook section "3. Cut a release". origin/main == origin/dev == 2cca01dd at filing; the root manifest read 0.14.1 then; the 0.14.1 cut was LCLI-714. The "<= 0.14.1"/"pre-0.14.2" wording in #691 assumed the original version number; the shipped pre-0.14.2 test title is now pre-0.15.0. Do not start the bump until the leader briefs the metadata PR (after quest-cli bump is on quest-cli main). Known carried items: LCLI-760 macOS wedge on main CI (not a gate here), LCLI-773 setup-quest dead weight in the probe job, LCLI-482 OIDC.

acceptanceCriteria.text: LCLI-482 (OIDC trusted publishing) is read LIVE before the publish route is chosen, and the chosen route (publish-release.sh from the operator's machine vs a publish: true dispatch) is recorded here with that read's date.

(a) Metadata PR, after quest-cli's 0.15.0 bump is on quest-cli main: version bumped in root manifest, all six per-platform manifests under npm and root optionalDependencies in one commit; README version lines regenerated; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] cut to 0.15.0 carrying LCLI-771, LCLI-751 and LCLI-774; scripts/version-parity.mjs agrees with quest-cli main; merged to dev, promoted to main with the main CI matrix read by ref.

Probe note: this cut SHIPS LCLI-771, so the current release-gate probe (fresh writes .agents/skills/lore/SKILL.md, npm latest 0.14.1 exits 6 with the whole line `out-of-date .codex/skills/lore/SKILL.md`) is still expected to PASS; the publish=false dry run on the untagged ref proves that, and the re-base onto new binary behaviour is the NEXT release's precondition (docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md, 'Before tagging, re-base the release gate probe').

(b) The verified main commit is tagged v0.15.0 and the tag pushed; in the same sitting opum-marketplace is sent the tag name, tag object SHA, the commit it peels to and the resolved skills/ tree SHA (LCLI-469), to be re-resolved by them, and a second message when npm publishes.
(c) A release.yml publish=false dispatch on the tag (with launcher_rc set) succeeds: version-parity, all six release gate probe legs (both arms in the log), qualification; run id recorded.

(d) rc staging to the release-candidate dist-tag (six platforms at 0.15.0, launcher at 0.15.0-rc.N) via scripts/publish-release.sh with the version and the run id, --dry-run then for real: the operator's own dialog (tier 3, registry publication), never moved by relay or grant.

(e) opum-cli-e2e pair receipt lands for the staged pair; the `latest` move (quest first, then lore, scripts/promote-latest.mjs, on opum-agent's go) is the operator's own dialog (tier 3); the post-latest checklist (runbook item 8) is run and recorded.
LCLI-771 criterion 5 (the fix ships in a release) is satisfied and LCLI-771 can close once its criterion 1 (operator's Windows check) is also recorded.

implementationNotes: METADATA STAGE (2026-10-31, branch chore/LCLI-775-bump-0.14.2, held for review, not landed): bumps package.json, six npm platform manifests, root optionalDependencies pins, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, bun.lock pins (6 lines; lock has 0 resolved lore entries so the hand edit equals a regen; check:lockfile-pins agrees), README via shipped-readme-version.mjs --write (--check exit 0), CHANGELOG [Unreleased] folded into ## [0.14.2] - 2026-10-31 plus a LCLI-776 macOS pin entry (all of [Unreleased] ships, including LCLI-765, LCLI-740/762, LCLI-689 and the resume fix, not only ODOC-556; date is today and may need changing at tag), the declared Quest version token in CLAUDE.md managed block line 268, the two Ladybug fixture canonicalExportSha256 baselines and the report test baseline (only canonicalExportSha256 moved; negative control with only package.json reverted passes against the old baselines), and test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts to 0.14.2. Parity gate measured both directions: lore 0.14.2 vs quest main 0.14.1 REFUSE; lore 0.14.1 vs quest 0.14.2 REFUSE; 0.14.2 vs 0.14.2 OK. quest-cli main and dev read 0.14.1 and npm quest is latest 0.14.1 / rc 0.14.1-rc.1 when read. Expected reds until quest 0.14.2 is on npm: lore check exits 6 on the runtime pair lock; 3 tests in test/link-quest-race.test.ts that drive real quest fail on the same lock.

ODOC-556 ruling (opum-doc, 2026-10-31 ~08:12Z): the pair ships as 0.15.0, not 0.14.2. Codex skill path move marked breaking under 0.15.0 in CHANGELOG (the Changed (breaking) heading is the marker scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs reads). Gate measured both ways: red at 0.14.2 (breaking heading, patch bump), green at 0.15.0 (0.14.1 to 0.15.0 minor). Benchmark fixture digests regenerated (they embed the version). Upgrade step in the entry is plain lore agents then delete the old .codex skill by hand; lore agents has no --update-instructions flag (that is quest).

Final-head commit: QUEST_SOURCE_REF in ci.yml pinned to quest-cli dev squash 81645e55 (#709, QCLI-551, 0.15.0), resolved against the remote first; source-ref passed at the 3 setup-quest call sites; CLAUDE.md managed block declares Quest 0.15.0 (version token only, quest binary here is 0.14.1 so no regeneration); release.yml untouched. Removal is LCLI-781 once quest 0.15.0 is on npm.

OPEN AMENDMENT 2026-11-01 (Opus review of lore-cli#702 at 5d54541, finding 2): the title, description and AC1, AC3, AC5 said 0.14.2 and are amended to 0.15.0, per dec-0kfl7kc (the operator marked 0.15.0 ready) and the ODOC-556 semver ruling. No criterion was ticked. Besides the version number, AC1 names the root and per-platform manifests instead of listing their paths, and AC5 says the version and the run id instead of angle-bracket placeholders (wording changed only to pass the shell guard). AC1 precondition (after quest-cli bump is on quest-cli MAIN) is left as written, the order of the pair landings being the leader call.

OPEN NOTE 2026-11-01, AC1 ticked: dev was promoted to main at eb13ece3 (fast-forward, PR 709) and the main CI matrix was read by ref: run 41276839527 on eb13ece3. Its one red job is lint typecheck test (macos-15), job 124760620187, the LCLI-760 wedge, accepted by the leader on the evidence in the LCLI-760 note (both attempts silent 120s at different tests, no assertion failure, a re-run adds no evidence). Every other job in that run is success or skipped by design (promotion is manual). The matrix was NOT all green. The Main fast-forward guard push run 41276839535 is success. LCLI-775 stays open for the cut.

AC0 READ 2026-11-01T14:xxZ-live (read at about 14:00Z): publish route = scripts/publish-release.sh run from the operator machine (granular npm token from the macOS Keychain, service npm-opum-ai-publish), NOT a publish: true dispatch. Live evidence: (1) LCLI-482 is To Do, title OIDC trusted publishing is broken by GitHub immutable subject claims, last amended 2026-09-18, still states release.yml with publish: true cannot publish and no release since 0.6.1 carries provenance. (2) npm registry, read today: @opum-ai/lore@0.14.1 (latest, published 2026-10-20), @opum-ai/quest@0.14.1 and @opum-ai/lore-linux-x64@0.14.1 all report NO dist.attestations. (3) every recent release.yml run (41172738034, 41161942219, both success) shows the OIDC publish job skipped, i.e. nothing has exercised OIDC since. (4) the Keychain entry npm-opum-ai-publish exists (attribute read only, secret never read; created and modified 2026-09-14), so the token is 48 days old against the 90-day granular-token cap: expiry is not readable without using the credential, and publish-release.sh own preflight is what proves it. LIMIT of this read: there is no cheap live test of OIDC; the only one is a publish: true dispatch, which stages packages and is tier 3. So this records that nothing shows OIDC repaired and the last known state is broken, not that it was re-proven broken today. LCLI-278 is Done, so a publish: true dispatch is not prohibited by it, but it cannot authenticate while LCLI-482 stands. Consequence to carry: the 0.15.0 launcher ships on latest with no provenance attestation, as 0.14.1 did.
